answer: In an agent economy, a bonded identity system resists Sybils by requiring each participant to lock a crystal-clear stake as collateral. Peers continuously grade behavior for uniqueness; coordinated fake accounts trigger automatic slashing of the bond. This works because an attacker must immobilize substantial capital across every identity, and rebuilding a credible history costs time and fees that grow linearly, making large-scale attacks uneconomical against the genuine reef of agents. A unique activity quill further raises the barrier.
